---
title: "Methods and source notes"
---

## Purpose

This project demonstrates a connected scientific workflow. Its intentionally broad title is a narrative device, not a tested conclusion. No text or figure was copied from a research paper.

## Public data

The source inventory, download addresses, source identifiers and checksums live in `data/allen/provenance.json` and the accompanying data README. Dataset records are cited in `references/library.bib`. Raw source files are retained so the plots can be rebuilt or replaced.

## Plot construction

Thirty-three editable SVG panels come from three generators: `scripts/generate-plots.py` makes the twelve original panels that the four native slides use; `scripts/advanced/population.py`, `tuning.py` and `architecture.py` make families 13–20, including two Data Morph sets; and `scripts/advanced/flagship.py` makes the thirteen journal-style panels behind the figures. `scripts/advanced/compose-flagship.sh` and `compose-structure.sh` rebuild Figure 1 and Figure 2 from those panels through the Flux command line, so the compositions are ordinary Flux files. Plot processing details are recorded by the generator and inventory. Network edges summarize response similarity; they should not be interpreted as measured synaptic connections. Population projections are descriptive views of the selected response matrix.

## Anatomy and physiology

Brain surfaces, neuronal reconstructions and population measurements provide complementary context. They may come from different public specimens or experiments. The project does not claim a matched multimodal recording.

## Details in the flagship panels

The anatomical insets intersect the bundled CCF surface meshes at two coronal planes (8.5 and 9.5 mm on the CCF anterior–posterior coordinate). They are outlines of the source surfaces, not histological images. The neuron panel pairs the original reconstructions with a three-dimensional Sholl profile: the number of intersections between dendritic segments and spheres at increasing distance from the soma.

In the response atlas, cells are grouped by their preferred drift direction. The colored trace above each stimulus block summarizes its preferred cohort (mean and standard error across cells); the gray envelope shows the 10th–90th percentile of the whole population. The heatmap retains the individual cells. These summaries describe the bundled example recording and do not imply a matched anatomy–activity experiment.

## Editing and reproducibility

Edit the manuscript in Paper, rearrange panels and labels in Figure, and edit the presentation in Slides. The shared plot sources live in `plots/`; accepted copies in `fig/assets/` are managed by Flux. Editing or regenerating a plot updates its linked placements. The website refresh command reads this project and rebuilds the public exports without replacing its authored documents or compositions.
